questions.question: When should you still advise Functional Skills to a Pass GCSE caller?
options: Never: they asked for a GCSE
Whenever it suits them. Only go for GCSE when Functional Skills isn't right
questions.explanation: Still advise Functional Skills to anyone it suits. Only go for GCSE when Functional Skills isn't right for them.

questions.question: Where and when are Pass GCSE exams sat?
options: In person at an exam centre, on set dates
questions.explanation: Exams are sat in person at an exam centre near the learner, on set dates: May, and November for resits.

questions.question: Who can sit in the November series?
options: Learners 16 or over, resits only (except IGCSE)
questions.explanation: In November learners must be 16 or over, and it's resits only except IGCSE, generally just maths and English.

questions.question: A maths learner doesn't know their exam board. Which do you use?
questions.explanation: For maths, if they don't know, use Edexcel, the most common.

questions.question: An English learner doesn't know their exam board. Which do you use?
questions.explanation: For English, if they don't know, use AQA.

questions.question: Once we offer a centre, how long does the learner have to confirm or decline it?
questions.explanation: Admin emails to check they're happy, and they must confirm or decline within 1 week. They get a reminder if not.

questions.question: Can you discount an exam-only Pass GCSE booking?
questions.explanation: No discount on exam-only bookings at all. The only discount is 10% off the course.

questions.question: How many hours of study per subject do we recommend on a Pass GCSE course?
questions.explanation: We recommend around 100 hours of study per subject.
